newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, supported by tight hog supplies, livestock dealers said.
Further gains were expected from continued strength in pork prices, particularly loins, which could increase packer demand, they said.

Central carlot pork prices were mixed on Monday, with fresh loins up $1.00 to $4.00 per cwt and butts up $3.00 to $4.00, USDA reported. Advances offset weakness in hams and pork belly prices, the statistics showed. There were 47.63 loads of pork cuts and 8.0 loads of trimmings sold.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs at the plant could range $59.50 to $60.00. Illinois top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range $58.50 to $59.50 and Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could span $59.00 to $59.50, livestock dealers said.
Gains in cash hog prices could be pared Tuesday amid forecasts for rain in the Midwest, which could result in a few extra hogs coming to market, they said.
Strength could also be limited by belief that prices are near a top and that retail pork demand is waning as retailers complete purchases for end-of-month features, they said.
